clue.text: Trotter's back, admitting work was not on the level

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the reversed name takes the other piece inside it
back tells us to read the possessive name from right to left

parts.note: Del Boy Trotter, of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, gives DEL'S
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A remark that a man named Trotter's back muscles were bent out of true.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; 'back' turns his possessive into SLED. 'Trotter' tempts towards pigs' feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sloped was tilted at an angle rather than horizontal, so it was not level.

clue.text: Windows removed after this order, at the end of the day?

definitions.text: order, at the end of the day?

parts.note: lights is an old word for windows, as in leaded lights
taken away, so out

explanation.surface: Blackout curtains come down once this command is given at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the evening command in a dormitory or barracks to put the lamps off; the wordplay pairs a word for windows with one for removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The call given at bedtime in a school or barracks to switch every lamp off.

clue.text: Randy old ruler briefly caught on film

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the ruler's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Priam was the ancient king of Troy
a pic is a picture, a film

explanation.surface: An elderly lustful monarch is quickly snapped by a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the M from PRIAM, King of Troy, leaving PRIA; 'caught on' just joins it to PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapic describes male sexual arousal, after the fertility god Priapus, so it means lustful.

clue.text: Away from public attention, guide leader is into good works

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
works as in a mechanism being worked over, signalling the letters of good are rearranged
leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide captain busies herself with charitable deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges GOOD into DOGO, and 'is into' places G, the leader of 'guide', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is to stay hidden and quiet, out of sight of everyone.

clue.text: I'm a fool to take charge of criminal investigation

parts.note: to head something is to lead or run it
a police inquiry is a case

explanation.surface: A detective admits he was silly to agree to lead the inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' frames the clue as the answer speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Headcase is British slang for an unstable or idiotic person.

clue.text: Enjoying oneself putting on a military display

definitions.meaning: taking great pleasure in a situation
a field day was originally a day of manoeuvres and review for troops

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means relishing an opportunity, and literally describes troops staging a day of exercises for review.

clue.text: Rand invested in new African-English travel company

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money placed in a business
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for the South African rand

explanation.surface: South African currency is put into a fresh Anglo-African transport business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AFRICAN into AIFRANC; 'invested in' puts R (rand) into it, then E for English ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Air France is the French national airline, a carrier of travellers.

clue.text: Man at last has raised pounds for clothes

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means a letter is shifted higher, nearer the top of the word

parts.note: a cobbler is a man who works at a last, the foot-shaped shoemaker's block
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A man who has finally collected money buys clothing with it.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped block, so 'Man at last' is a cobbler; 'has raised' moves the L of COBBLER up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing and gear.

clue.text: Labourer, one kept in line

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker has been held back in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter in many typefaces.

clue.text: Showing great enthusiasm when taking the plunge

definitions.meaning: literally jumping off a ship into the water

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for excess zeal literally means falling or leaping off a ship's side.

clue.text: Resign, now dept's reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quits now that their department has been restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to leave a post voluntarily.

clue.text: Snub a specialist in religious education

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: Someone cold-shoulders an expert in school divinity lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a blunt refusal or rejection, a cold dismissal.

clue.text: No doubt soldiers — reservists — will follow regimental leader home

indicators.note: will follow means this piece comes after the one before it

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
in means at home

explanation.surface: Without question, troops and part-timers will trail their commanding officer back to barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will follow' puts TA (the Territorial Army, British reservists) after R, the leader of 'regimental'.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain means definitely, beyond any question.

clue.text: Checked 19 again, as told

definitions.meaning: 19 is the answer numbers, so checking them again is counting once more

explanation.definitionFit: The word means counted a second time, or narrated a tale.

clue.text: TV presenter's crude introduction is cut

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: gross means coarse or crude

explanation.surface: A television host's vulgar opening remarks are edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction is cut' removes the G from GROSS; the presenter is Jonathan Ross, a British chat-show host.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Ross is a long-running British television host.

clue.text: One stops being more resolute

definitions.meaning: one who stops a flow, as of blood

explanation.definitionFit: To staunch is to stem a flow, and staunch also means steadfast, so this is its comparative.

clue.text: Sailor on street getting shot

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman in the road is hit by gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; 'shot' is the definition in the sense of having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab means having a go, an attempt.

clue.text: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed

definitions.text: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed

parts.words: Complete exhaustion? Result: a new start is needed
parts.note: describes total collapse from overwork, after which one must begin afresh

explanation.definitionFit: The term names physical or mental collapse caused by prolonged stress and overwork.

clue.text: Conflict, an atrocity to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Conflict, an atrocity to' (7,3) appears cut short: CRIME + AN gives CRIMEAN but nothing for WAR follows 'to', and a search found no fuller text.

clue.text: Songs from the sixties, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: Musical items in a performance are numbers, and the sixties are one band of figures.

clue.text: Glimpse what's stuck in paper cups

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside the following words

explanation.surface: A peek at what is clinging to the inside of disposable cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' points to letters running across 'paper cups'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief insight or quick view of something.

clue.text: Do down

parts.note: read as groom feathers, as a bird tidies its plumage, not as belittle

explanation.definitionFit: A bird preening itself smooths and tidies its feathers with its beak.

clue.text: Dressing to secure injured tissue

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the outer piece wraps around the inner

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds
game means lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A bandage is applied to protect damaged flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like the definition (a bandage), but it gives the outer piece; GAME for injured is an old use, as in a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of fibrous connective tissue joining bones.

clue.text: Cigarette smoking initially banned: one looks surprised

indicators.note: banned means excluded, so a letter is removed

parts.note: gasper is old British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Once tobacco is prohibited, someone stares in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: GASPER is old British slang for a cheap cigarette; 'banned' removes the S taken by 'initially' from 'smoking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is a person staring open-mouthed in wonder.

clue.text: Distorted version of prophet's decree, not the actual words

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: A garbled account of a seer's edict misquotes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect speech reports what someone said without quoting them verbatim.

clue.text: Tune idly composed in harmonious style

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A melody is lazily written so that it sounds sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting unitedly means acting together in agreement.

clue.text: Rearrange where to go on holiday

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-sort it means sort again; it also names a holiday destination.
